tasks.title: Clean the Broken Customer Export
tasks.context: Operations received a vendor export that will feed a customer KPI report. The file contains missing values, duplicates, inconsistent categories, mixed date formats and suspicious numeric values.
tasks.goal: Choose every cleaning action that should happen before analysis.
tasks.deliverable: Select the complete defensible cleaning plan. Do not invent replacements for unknown values.
tasks.prompt: Which actions should you take? Select all that apply.
expectedSelections: Remove the exact duplicate O-1002 row after confirming it is a duplicate.
Treat blank or non-numeric ages as invalid/missing and flag them for a defined remediation rule.
Standardize north, North and NORTH into one canonical region value.
Parse the mixed date strings into one validated date format.
Investigate the -999 amount as an invalid value or outlier before using it in KPIs.
hints: Look for repeated business keys, missing/invalid fields, inconsistent labels, mixed formats and implausible numbers.
Cleaning should preserve uncertainty. Do not silently guess a missing customer name or age.
There are five valid actions: duplicate handling, age validation, region standardization, date parsing and negative-amount investigation.
tasks.explanation: A robust cleaning workflow identifies the issue, applies a documented rule, validates the result and preserves an audit trail. Guessing missing values or deleting every unusual row can create bias.
options: Remove the exact duplicate O-1002 row after confirming it is a duplicate.
Treat blank or non-numeric ages as invalid/missing and flag them for a defined remediation rule.
Standardize north, North and NORTH into one canonical region value.
Parse the mixed date strings into one validated date format.
Investigate the -999 amount as an invalid value or outlier before using it in KPIs.
Replace every missing customer name with the most common customer name.
Delete every row that looks unusual without documenting why.
